attempts.paper_title: Transformation of a Spatial Map across the Hippocampal-Lateral Septal Circuit
attempts.entry_title: Spike phase coding in the lateral septum (Tingley and Buzsaki 2018)
attempts.summary: The paper's central claim, that lateral septum neurons encode position better in the theta phase of their spikes than in their firing rate, did not hold up in this data, nor did the equivalence of rate and phase codes in hippocampal place fields. The likely reason is a step the paper does not describe: how position bins with no nearby spike, about 70% of samples, enter phase decoding. As reported, the septal phase code was more reliable across the population than hippocampal codes, and theta coherence and coupling with CA3 rose along the run. The depth gradient held under one analysis reading only, hippocampal-septal assemblies did not match the paper's, and the spiking model was not run.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Tingley and Buzsaki (2018) on dandiset 000213, which holds silicon probe recordings from the lateral septum and the dorsal hippocampus of five rats running on mazes. It decodes position from single-unit rates and theta phases, defines place fields, measures spatial information, relates phase coding to recording depth and running speed, and measures CA1-LS and CA3-LS theta coherence and theta-gamma coupling along the run. Peer prediction of cell assemblies is run on a random sample of hippocampal-LS pairs.

proposed.reason: The verifier found readings chosen inconsistently: fig4d was judged on whichever decoder reading passes, fig1i on the adopted aa1 alone. One rule now decides every claim, the one the claims file uses throughout (a criterion is met under one reading): with undefined phase 0 and ties at random, the 1.5 cm reading ab1 with rate map (b) gives KS p = 0.066 over 1,924 place fields and 0.82 over 45 sessions, neither below 0.05 (notebook, fig1i cell, line under the table). Under the other 7 readings at least one test gives p < 0.05, so the reproduction is fragile. The verifier did not agree in round 3 and gives not_reproduced: the criterion has no "under one reading" clause and says "Reproduced when neither test gives p < 0.05; not reproduced when either does"; for a claim of absence a pass under any of 8 readings grows easier with each reading added; the rule was chosen after the per-reading results were known; ab1 is only partly a 1.5 cm reading, as 2,822 of its 5,723 hippocampal conditions keep 201 bins and take the aa1 result; and each criterion should be applied as written. The outcome is kept.

paper_notes.statement: Question for the authors. In the single-cell phase decoder, how does a trial's position bin enter when no spike falls in its 20-bin smoothing window, so that its phase is undefined? About 70% of trial-by-bin samples are affected, and STAR Methods, position prediction analysis, does not say. Left out, the decoder reads where the cell fires: phases shifted within trials beat rate in 0.21 to 0.54 of conditions, and LS phase then beats rate as reported. Set to phase 0, shifted phases beat rate in 0.026 to 0.060 of conditions, about 3 to 6 times the nominal 1% but below the real 0.044 to 0.082; LS phase no longer beats rate, and hippocampal phase is slightly worse than rate. At fine smoothing the fill makes phase information measure whether a spike is near. Neither treatment gives a working hippocampal phase decoder (aa1 real phase MSE 6,573, shifted 6,641, chance 6,707). Under both, the comparison with permuted chance passes shifted phases nearly as often as real ones.

Question for the authors. How is the Olypher peak information converted to bits/cm (Results, paragraph 4, 0.4 against 1.7 bits/cm), and are the 7 levels of equal width or equal count? Neither reading tried gives both averages.
The 1,425 hippocampal neurons of the place-field definition (STAR Methods) are not identified. Units with at least one included condition number 1,420 in the files, which may be the set meant.
Results, paragraph 1 gives 1,587 CA1 and 224 CA3 place fields (1,811 in all), while Figures 1 and 2 use 1,820 place fields.

Question for the authors. In the single-cell decoder, which bin is predicted when several template bins are equally near the test value (many bins of a rate template are 0 Hz)? A first-index rule sends all of them to the lowest bin and puts the hippocampal rate MSE above uniform guessing (median 7,537 against 6,733 bins squared); random choice gives 6,329.

Question for the authors. In peer prediction, is the GLM fitted per trial or over the condition's concatenated trials, and how are trials of different lengths paired in the trial-order shuffles? Which pairs make up the 11,264 examined? This attempt finds 81,393 pairs with both units included in the condition.

bz_phaseMap2Bins, which makeFig4.m (DavidTingley/papers at 9f4cd48) calls to bin spike phases for Figure 4, is in none of the public repositories, neither buzsakilab/buzcode at e615663 or its current master nor DavidTingley/scratch at 2f80453.

entries.title: Spike phase coding in the lateral septum (Tingley and Buzsaki 2018)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Tingley and Buzsaki (2018) on dandiset 000213, which holds silicon probe recordings from the lateral septum and the dorsal hippocampus of five rats running on mazes. It decodes position from single-unit rates and theta phases, defines place fields, measures spatial information, relates phase coding to recording depth and running speed, and measures CA1-LS and CA3-LS theta coherence and theta-gamma coupling along the run. Peer prediction of cell assemblies is run on a random sample of hippocampal-LS pairs.
